deities: Sree Bhadrakali (Jagadambika, the Goddess of Oodanadu)
festivals: Kumbha Bharani (Chettikulangara Bharani, Malayalam month of Kumbham, February-March; Bharani nakshatra day)
Kettukazhcha (night procession of towering chariot structures - six Kuthira horse effigies of 70-75 ft, five Theru chariots, and giant Bhima, Hanuman and Panchali figures built by the 13 Karas)
Kuthiyottam (ceremonial dance-song ritual performed by young boys)
Chanthattam (signature offering ritual; the 1001-lamp stone deepasthambham blazes during evening Deeparadhana)

history.dynasty: None attested (tradition links Venad rulers - Samudra Bandhan, courtier of Ravi Varman, and King Adithya Kulasekharan, 1347-1389, are said to have visited)
history.period: Traditionally 843 CE (Makara, Uttrattadi) by Padmapada Acharya, disciple of Adi Shankaracharya; popular belief says over 1200 years old
history.summary: Chettikulangara Sree Bhagavathi Temple, dedicated to Sree Bhadrakali as Jagadambika, the Goddess of Oodanadu, is one of the 108 Durga temples tradition attributes to Parasurama and one of his five Ambalayas; it is administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board as its second-highest revenue temple after Sabarimala. The popular origin legend says local chieftains, humiliated when they visited the Koypallikarazhma Bhagavathi temple festival, resolved to build their own Bhagavathi temple; led by the Karanavars of the leading families (Chembolil Thangal, Puthupurakkal Unnithan, Kaitha Thekku Mangattachan, Mecheril Panickar) they performed 12 days of Bhajanam at Kodungallur, received a dream-vision of the Goddess, and returned with a sacred sword given by Kodungallur's Velichappadu to begin construction. One scholarly tradition holds the temple was consecrated in 843 CE (Makara month, Uttrattadi nakshatra) by Padmapada Acharya, a disciple of Adi Shankaracharya - though no firm epigraphic record fixes the date. The temple's most famous tradition, the Kettukazhcha, is about 180-200 years old: village chieftains stranded on the Kollam-Chavara canal works vowed to build giant offering structures for Bhagavathy if they were allowed home, and began the annual procession once they returned.

name: Chettikulangara Devi Temple
town_description: Chettikulangara is a temple town in Mavelikkara taluk of Alappuzha district, in the Onattukara region of central Kerala, about 5 km from Mavelikkara town and 45 km south of Alappuzha. It is defined by the Sree Bhagavathi temple and its 13 Karas (territorial divisions), which rally every year for the famous Kumbha Bharani festival and its monumental Kettukazhcha chariot pageant.

travel.airport: Trivandrum International Airport (approx. 110-120 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Mavelikkara Railway Station (approx. 5 km); Kayamkulam Junction (approx. 6-8 km), well connected across Kerala.
travel.road: On the Kayamkulam-Mavelikkara route, about 8 km from Kayamkulam and 45 km south of Alappuzha town; autos, buses and taxis run from Mavelikkara and Kayamkulam.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Kumbha Bharani (February-March, usually the first week of March) is the most spectacular time but draws lakhs of devotees - book travel and stay well ahead; weekday mornings are quietest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily morning 5:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify - some sources list 4:30 AM opening or 8:30 PM close, and hours extend during festivals). Traditional attire required (dhoti/mundu for men, saree or salwar for women); footwear not allowed; photography prohibited inside the sanctum.
